output.claims_about_policy: The key policy point is scope. The stated policy bars certification without material caveats unless either no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation exists with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible record does not satisfy that clean-certification predicate because the runbook is still draft and threshold/review date are TBD, and the refund-workflow issue remains unresolved. At the same time, the policy text the auditor cites does not require treating every certification request as escalatory failure; it permits a narrower outcome in which the certification packet is understood as a qualified governance case with explicit disclosure of the named limitation. Aggregate readiness and general risk-management guidance do not cure the missing approval elements, but they do support reducing overbreadth in the actor claim from clean compliance to caveated compliance.

output.final_rationale: The verdict changes only because the Actor narrowed the claim from an overbroad clean-certification position to a policy-bounded, caveated one using the same admissible record. No genuinely new admissible evidence was added. Under the stated policy, clean certification is not supportable because the record still shows a remaining material weakness and an incomplete draft mitigation. But the policy text, as provided here, specifically bars certification without material caveats unless the weakness is resolved or an approved mitigation exists. On this record, a narrower outcome is supportable: aggregate readiness may be certified only as a qualified governance case that explicitly discloses the refund-workflow limitation, not as evidence of full remediation or unconditional compliance. That is why the proper outcome is compliant_with_caveats rather than compliant or noncompliant.
